chapter.li: Verse13 And when Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say that I, the Son of Man, am? VerseEnd Verse14 And they said, Some say John the Baptist, some Elijah, and others Jeremiah, or one of the prophets. VerseEnd Verse15 He said unto them, But whom do you say that I am? VerseEnd Verse16 And Simon Peter answered and said, You are the Christ, the Son of the living God. VerseEnd Verse17 And Jesus answered and said unto him, Blessed are you, Simon Barjona, for flesh and blood has not revealed this unto you, but my Father who is in Heaven. VerseEnd Verse18 And I say also unto you that you are Peter. And upon this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. VerseEnd Verse19 And I will give unto you the keys of the kingdom of Heaven, and whatever you shall bind on earth shall be bound in Heaven, and whatever you shall set loose on earth shall be set loose in Heaven. VerseEnd Verse20 Then charged he his disciples that they should tell no man that he was Jesus, the Christ. VerseEnd

Verse21 From that time forth began Jesus to show unto his disciples that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders, and chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day. VerseEnd Verse22 Then Peter took him and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from you, Lord. This shall not be done unto you. VerseEnd Verse23 But he turned and said unto Peter, Get behind me, Satan. You are an offense unto me, for you savor not the things that are of God, but those that are of men. VerseEnd

Verse24 Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. And now, for a man to take up his cross is to deny himself from all ungodliness, and from every worldly lust, and keep my commandments. VerseEnd Verse25 Break not my commandments to save your lives, for whoever will save his life in this world shall lose it in the world to come. And whoever will lose his life in this world, for my sake, shall find it in the world to come. Therefore, forsake the world and save your souls. VerseEnd Verse26 For what is a man profited if he shall gain the whole world and lose his own soul? Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul? VerseEnd Verse27 For the Son of Man shall come in the glory of his Father, with his angels, and then he shall reward every man according to his works. VerseEnd Verse28 Truly I say unto you, there are some standing here who shall not taste of death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom. VerseEnd

LEChapter17 Verse1 And after six days, Jesus took Peter, James, and John his brother, and brought them up into a high mountain apart, VerseEnd Verse2 and was transfigured before them. And his face did shine as the sun and his raiment was white as the light. VerseEnd Verse3 And behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him. VerseEnd Verse4 Then answered Peter and said unto Jesus, Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you are willing, let us make here three tabernacles: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elias. VerseEnd Verse5 While he yet spoke, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. And behold, a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my Beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear him. VerseEnd Verse6 And when the disciples heard the voice, they fell on their faces and were sorely afraid. VerseEnd Verse7 And Jesus came and touched them, and said, Arise, and be not afraid. VerseEnd Verse8 And when they had lifted up their eyes, they saw no man save Jesus only. VerseEnd

Verse9 And as they came down from the mountain, Jesus charged them, saying, Tell the vision to no man until the Son of Man is risen again from the dead. VerseEnd Verse10 And his disciples asked him, saying, Why then say the scribes that Elias must first come? VerseEnd Verse11 And Jesus answered and said unto them, Elias truly shall first come and restore all things, VerseEnd Verse12 as the prophets have written. And again I say unto you that Elias has come already — concerning whom it is written: Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me — and they knew him not, and have done unto him whatever they desired. Likewise shall also the Son of Man suffer of them. But I say unto you, who is Elias? Behold, this is Elias: whom I send to prepare the way before me. VerseEnd Verse13 Then the disciples understood that he spoke unto them of John the Baptist, and also of another who should come and restore all things, as it is written by the prophets. VerseEnd

Verse14 And when they had come to the multitude, there came to him a man, kneeling down to him and saying, VerseEnd Verse15 Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is lunatic and severely vexed, for ofttimes he falls into the fire and oft into the water. VerseEnd Verse16 And I brought him to your disciples and they could not cure him. VerseEnd Verse17 Then Jesus answered and said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I suffer you? Bring him here to me. VerseEnd Verse18 And Jesus rebuked the devil and he departed out of him. And the child was cured from that very hour. VerseEnd

Verse19 Then came the disciples to Jesus apart, and said, Why could we not cast him out? VerseEnd Verse20 And Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief. For truly I say unto you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you shall say unto this mountain, Remove to that place — and it shall move; and nothing shall be impossible unto you. VerseEnd Verse21 Nevertheless, this kind goes not out but by prayer and fasting. VerseEnd

Verse22 And while they abided in Galilee, Jesus said unto them, The Son of Man shall be betrayed into the hands of men, VerseEnd Verse23 and they shall kill him, and the third day he shall be raised again. And they were exceedingly sorry. VerseEnd

Verse24 And when they had come to Capernaum, they that received tribute came to Peter and said, Does not your master pay tribute? VerseEnd Verse25 He said, Yes. And when he had come into the house, Jesus rebuked him, saying, What do you think, Simon? Of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? Of their own children or of strangers? VerseEnd Verse26 Peter said unto him, Of strangers. Jesus said unto him, Then are the children free. VerseEnd Verse27 Notwithstanding, lest we should offend them, go to the sea, and cast a hook, and take up the fish that first comes up. And when you have opened his mouth, you shall find a piece of money. That take, and give unto them for me and you. VerseEnd

LEChapter18 Verse1 At the same time came the disciples unto Jesus, saying, Who is the greatest in the kingdom of Heaven? VerseEnd Verse2 And Jesus called a little child unto him, and set him in the middle of them, VerseEnd Verse3 and said, Truly I say unto you, except you are converted and become as little children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of Heaven. VerseEnd Verse4 Whoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of Heaven. VerseEnd Verse5 And whoever shall receive one such little child in my name, receives me. VerseEnd Verse6 But whoever shall offend one of these little ones who believe in me, it would be better for him that a millstone were hung about his neck and he was drowned in the depth of the sea. VerseEnd

Verse7 Woe unto the world because of offenses, for it must be that offenses come, but woe to that man by whom the offense comes. VerseEnd Verse8 Wherefore, if your hand or your foot offend you, cut it off and cast it from yourself, for it is better for you to enter into life lame or maimed, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into Everlasting fire. VerseEnd Verse9 And if your eye offend you, pluck it out and cast it from yourself. It is better for you to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into hellfire. And a man’s hand is his friend, and his foot also. And a man’s eye are they of his own household. VerseEnd

Verse10 Take heed that you despise not one of these little ones, for I say unto you that in Heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father who is in Heaven. VerseEnd Verse11 For the Son of Man has come to save that which was lost and to call sinners to repentance, but those little ones have no need of repentance, and I will save them. VerseEnd Verse12 What do you think? If a man have a hundred sheep, and one of them has gone astray, does he not leave the ninety-nine, and go into the mountains, and seek that which is gone astray? VerseEnd Verse13 And if it so be that he find it, truly I say unto you, he rejoices more over that which was lost than over the ninety-nine which went not astray. VerseEnd Verse14 Even so, it is not the will of your Father who is in Heaven that one of these little ones should perish. VerseEnd

Verse15 Moreover, if your brother shall trespass against you, go and tell him his fault between you and him alone. If he shall hear you, you have gained your brother. VerseEnd Verse16 But if he will not hear you, then take with you one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established. VerseEnd Verse17 And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church. But if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto you as a heathen man and a publican. VerseEnd

Verse18 Truly I say unto you, whatever you shall bind on earth shall be bound in Heaven, and whatever you shall set loose on earth shall be set loose in Heaven. VerseEnd Verse19 Again, I say unto you that if two of you shall agree on earth as touching anything that they shall ask, that they may not ask amiss, it shall be done for them of my Father who is in Heaven; VerseEnd Verse20 for where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them. VerseEnd

Verse21 Then came Peter to him and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times? VerseEnd Verse22 Jesus said unto him, I say not unto you, until seven times, but, until seventy times seven. VerseEnd Verse23 Therefore is the kingdom of Heaven likened unto a certain king who would take account of his servants; VerseEnd Verse24 and when he had begun to reckon, one was brought unto him who owed him ten thousand talents. VerseEnd Verse25 But forasmuch as he had nothing to pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made. VerseEnd Verse26 And the servant implored him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay you all. VerseEnd Verse27 Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and released him, and forgave him the debt. The servant therefore fell down and worshipped him. VerseEnd

Verse28 But the same servant went out and found one of his fellow servants, who owed him a hundred pence. And he laid hands on him and took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that you owe. VerseEnd Verse29 And his fellow servant fell down at his feet and implored him, saying, Have patience with me, and I will pay you all. VerseEnd Verse30 And he would not, but went and cast him into prison until he should pay the debt. VerseEnd

Verse31 So when his fellow servants saw what was done, they were very sorry, and came and told unto their lord all that was done. VerseEnd Verse32 Then his lord, after he had called him, said unto him, O you wicked servant, I forgave you all that debt because you desired me to. VerseEnd Verse33 Should you not also have had compassion on your fellow servant, even as I had pity on you? VerseEnd Verse34 And his lord was angry, and delivered him to the torturers until he should pay all that was due unto him. VerseEnd Verse35 So likewise shall my Heavenly Father do also unto you, if you from your hearts forgive not everyone his brother their trespasses. VerseEnd

LEChapter19 Verse1 And it came to pass, when Jesus had finished these sayings, he departed from Galilee and came into the borders of Judea beyond Jordan. VerseEnd Verse2 And great multitudes followed him, and many believed on him, and he healed them there. VerseEnd

Verse3 The Pharisees came also unto him, testing him, and saying unto him, Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for every cause? VerseEnd Verse4 And he answered and said unto them, Have you not read that he who made man at the beginning made him male and female, VerseEnd Verse5 and said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife, and they two shall be one flesh? VerseEnd Verse6 Wherefore, they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let not man put asunder. VerseEnd Verse7 They say unto him, Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement and to put her away? VerseEnd Verse8 He said unto them, Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, suffered you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it was not so. VerseEnd Verse9 And I say unto you, whoever shall divorce his wife, except for fornication, and shall marry another, commits adultery. And whoever marries her that is divorced does commit adultery. VerseEnd

Verse10 His disciples said unto him, If the case of the man should be so with a wife, it is not good to marry. VerseEnd Verse11 But he said unto them, All cannot receive this saying. It is not for them save to whom it is given. VerseEnd Verse12 For there are some eunuchs who were so born from their mother’s womb. And there are some eunuchs who were made eunuchs of men. And there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of Heaven’s sake. He that is able to receive, let him receive my sayings. VerseEnd

Verse13 Then were there brought unto him little children, that he should put hands on them and pray. And the disciples rebuked them, saying, There is no need, for Jesus has said such shall be saved. VerseEnd Verse14 But Jesus said, Suffer little children to come unto me and forbid them not, for of such is the kingdom of Heaven. VerseEnd Verse15 And he laid hands on them and departed from there. VerseEnd

Verse16 And behold, one came and said, Good Master, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life? VerseEnd Verse17 And he said unto him, Why do you call me good? There is none good but one — that is, God. But if you will enter into life, keep the commandments. VerseEnd Verse18 He said unto him, Which? Jesus said, You shall not kill. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal. You shall not bear false witness. VerseEnd Verse19 Honor your father and mother. And you shall love your neighbor as yourself. VerseEnd Verse20 The young man said unto him, All these things have I kept from my youth up. What lack I yet? VerseEnd Verse21 Jesus said unto him, If you will be perfect, go sell that you have and give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in Heaven; and come and follow me. VerseEnd Verse22 But when the young man heard that saying, he went away sorrowful, for he had great possessions. VerseEnd

Verse23 Then said Jesus unto his disciples, Truly I say unto you that a rich man shall difficultly enter into the kingdom of Heaven. VerseEnd Verse24 And again I say unto you, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. VerseEnd Verse25 When his disciples heard this, they were exceedingly amazed, saying, Who then can be saved? VerseEnd Verse26 But Jesus beheld their thoughts and said unto them, With men, this is impossible; but if they will forsake all things for my sake, with God, whatever things I speak are possible. VerseEnd

Verse27 Then answered Peter and said unto him, Behold, we have forsaken all and followed you. What shall we have therefore? VerseEnd Verse28 And Jesus said unto them, Truly I say unto you that you who have followed me shall, in the resurrection, when the Son of Man shall come sitting on the throne of his glory, you also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel. VerseEnd Verse29 And everyone that has forsaken houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name’s sake, shall receive a hundredfold and shall inherit everlasting life. VerseEnd Verse30 But many of the first shall be last, and the last, first. VerseEnd

LEChapter20 Verse1 For the kingdom of Heaven is like unto a man, a householder, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers into his vineyard. VerseEnd Verse2 And when he had agreed with the laborers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard. VerseEnd Verse3 And he went out about the third hour and found others standing idle in the marketplace, VerseEnd Verse4 and said unto them, Go also into the vineyard, and whatever is right, I will give you. And they went their way. VerseEnd Verse5 Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hour and did likewise. VerseEnd Verse6 And about the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing idle, and said unto them, Why stand you here all the day idle? VerseEnd Verse7 They say unto him, Because no man has hired us. He said unto them, Go also into the vineyard, and whatever is right, you shall receive. VerseEnd

Verse8 So when evening came, the lord of the vineyard said unto his steward, Call the laborers and give them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first. VerseEnd Verse9 And when they came that began about the eleventh hour, they received every man a penny. VerseEnd Verse10 But when the first came, they supposed that they should have received more. And they likewise received every man a penny. VerseEnd Verse11 And when they had received a penny, they murmured against the master of the house, VerseEnd Verse12 saying, These last have wrought one hour only, and you have made them equal unto us who have borne the burden and the heat of the day. VerseEnd Verse13 But he answered one of them and said, Friend, I do you no wrong. Did not you agree with me for a penny? VerseEnd Verse14 Take yours and go your way. I will give unto this last even as unto you. VerseEnd Verse15 Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with my own? Is your eye evil because I am good? VerseEnd Verse16 So the last shall be first, and the first, last. And many are called, but few chosen. VerseEnd
